ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Abrupt wheeze during a snack

A previously well 2-year-old suddenly coughs and chokes while eating peanuts. Ten minutes later, he has persistent right-sided wheeze and reduced right air entry without fever. Which diagnosis best explains the abrupt onset and focal examination?

  1. Bronchial foreign body aspiration
  2. First episode of diffuse asthma
  3. Viral bronchiolitis
  4. Lobar bacterial pneumonia
  5. Allergic rhinitis
Answer and explanation

Bronchial foreign body aspiration

A witnessed choking event followed by focal lower-airway findings strongly suggests an aspirated object.

Option explanations

Bronchial foreign body aspiration: A witnessed choking event followed by focal lower-airway findings strongly suggests an aspirated object.

First episode of diffuse asthma: Asthma usually causes diffuse rather than abruptly focal findings after choking.

Viral bronchiolitis: Bronchiolitis typically follows a viral prodrome and produces more diffuse signs.

Lobar bacterial pneumonia: Pneumonia does not usually begin within minutes of a choking event.

Allergic rhinitis: Rhinitis does not cause unilateral reduced air entry.
